rationale: Research handoff folding the second snapshot scenario into the behavior and Fact that own the mechanism. The draft map (base version 16) adds one branch note to b-install-snapshot-align and narrows the f-log-snapshot-agreement unknown to the premises the executions leave open, including the trailing-log-guard question; no trigger, guard, write, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changes, so the five violated scenarios, the two corroborating scenarios and all accepted results keep their original basis.

feedback.answered: The snapshot alignment finding now has two violated scenarios and a measured operational consequence. The first (execution 3d53c8e2) showed the install retains and reports an unconfirmed tail; the second (execution b9d811ad) showed the sharper effect: because the retained tail keeps the anchor index from being the effective last entry, the AppendEntries the leader sends after a successful install - anchored at the snapshot index - was rejected (append_success false) and the tail was left unchanged. The very request that was supposed to truncate the tail therefore could not, which is why the protocol's requirement to discard the log at install time matters rather than being a stylistic preference. Both scenarios completed with matched prerequisites and full comparisons, and both carry correspondence no_issue_found.
remaining: Real-leader reachability of the retained-tail state, and how long the rejection lasts before the leader's nextIndex walk or another snapshot changes it, are unmeasured.

Reachability with the default configuration is now characterised from source rather than executed: installSnapshot's compaction is skipped entirely when the receiver's log end is at or below TrailingLogs, and when it runs the bound is min(snapshot index, log end - TrailingLogs), so the anchor is deleted while a tail survives only if the snapshot index sits at least TrailingLogs below the log end. Whether a real leader drives a follower into that shape was not executed.

The other three findings keep their open premises: reachability of an out-of-window heartbeat sender, reachability of an unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, and whether batching FSMs are exempt from ConfigurationStore.

Leads with no obligation: ReloadConfig notification scope, the processHeartbeat concurrency contract, and the transport TimeoutScale configuration discrepancy. The in-memory snapshot store is still unread.
feedback.rationale: The second scenario's consequence belongs with the mechanism that produces it, so it is recorded as a branch note and reflected in the Fact's unknown rather than duplicated into the overview or the claim. The core overview, all four claims and every accepted result are unchanged.

b-install-snapshot-align.rationale: Adds one branch note carrying the measured consequence of the second scenario of the same requirement (execution b9d811ad): with a tail retained above the installed index the anchor is no longer the effective last entry, so the AppendEntries a leader sends next was rejected and the tail stayed, which means the deferral can block resumption of replication. Trigger, guards, writes, producers/consumers and the Fact it produces are unchanged.

f-log-snapshot-agreement.rationale: Narrows the Fact's unknown to the premises the two executions leave open and records the sourced reachability condition: installSnapshot's compaction is skipped when the receiver's log end is at or below TrailingLogs and otherwise removes entries only up to min(snapshot index, log end - TrailingLogs), so anchor deletion with a surviving tail requires the snapshot index to sit at least TrailingLogs below the log end. Meaning, identity, validity context, durability and recovery are unchanged.
